chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Habib, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Allah has assigned four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, to weep over him until the Day of Judgment. Visiting his grave is equivalent to performing a Hajj and an 'Umrah and (visiting) the graves of the martyrs.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition to emphasize the cosmic significance of Karbala, where the continuous weeping of four thousand angels underscores the eternal mourning for Imam al-Husayn (a.s.). This narration elevates the physical act of Ziyarah to a supreme spiritual merit, equating it with the combined rewards of Hajj, 'Umrah, and the visitation of martyrs' graves, thereby validating the shrine as a focal point of divine grace.
